   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e1bbfcb3",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Modeling the pupillometric signal\n",
    "\n",
    "The algorithms in this notebook, together with simulation studies showing their advantage over more traditional approaches, are described in\n",
    "\n",
    "> Mittner, M., & Groot, J. M. (2025). A novel method for modeling tonic and phasic pupil dynamics in humans. *Behavior Research Methods*, 57(9), 233. <https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-025-02755-7>\n",
    "\n",
    "Please cite this paper if you use `pupil.estimate_baseline()` or `pupil.estimate_response()`."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "1b7e03cd",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-10T13:34:34.779740Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-10T13:34:34.779594Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-10T13:34:35.882330Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-10T13:34:35.881405Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import pypillometry as pp\n",
    "from pypillometry import u\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import scipy.stats"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "06db3889",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "It can be useful to think about the pupillometric signal as being composed of different components. One common assumption, based on the finding that the pupil reflects activity in the norepinephrinergic system, is that it consists of slow, tonic (baseline) and faster, phasic (response) fluctuations.\n",
    "\n",
    "To illustrate this, we simulate data according to such a model: event-induced responses are superimposed on a slow, baseline-like component. The response to each event is a scaled version of a \"response kernel\" (Hoeks & Levelt, 1993), which can be plotted with `pp.signal.plot_prf()`:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "4e870597",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-10T13:34:35.884424Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-10T13:34:35.884110Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-10T13:34:36.051689Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-10T13:34:36.050873Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 600x300 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "plt.figure(figsize=(6, 3))\n",
    "pp.signal.plot_prf(npar=10.1, tmax=930);"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "25dd5d87",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "We create 100 events with random inter-stimulus intervals between 0.6 and 1.4 seconds (a \"fast\" paradigm in which the responses to successive events overlap), a slowly fluctuating baseline (`pp.signal.fake_pupil_baseline()`), a response of random amplitude to each event (using the design matrix from `pp.signal.pupil_build_design_matrix()`) and some measurement noise:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "id": "dd0b4522",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-10T13:34:36.054073Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-10T13:34:36.053913Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-10T13:34:36.383054Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-10T13:34:36.382022Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 1500x500 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "rng = np.random.default_rng(12)\n",
    "fs = 50       # sampling rate (Hz)\n",
    "ntrials = 100\n",
    "\n",
    "event_onsets = 2000 + np.cumsum(rng.uniform(600, 1400, ntrials))  # in ms\n",
    "duration = event_onsets[-1] + 5000                                   # in ms\n",
    "\n",
    "# time (ms) and baseline\n",
    "tx, real_baseline, _ = pp.signal.fake_pupil_baseline(duration/1000, fs, mean=1000, amplitude=100,\n",
    "                                              freq=0.1, seed=12)\n",
    "X = pp.signal.pupil_build_design_matrix(tx, event_onsets, fs, npar=10.1, tmax=930)\n",
    "real_response_coef = rng.uniform(50, 150, ntrials)\n",
    "real_response = real_response_coef @ X\n",
    "noise = rng.normal(0, 5, len(tx))\n",
    "\n",
    "faked = pp.EyeData(left_pupil=real_baseline + real_response + noise, time=tx,\n",
    "                   event_onsets=event_onsets, event_labels=[\"event\"]*ntrials,\n",
    "                   name=\"simulated\")\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.figure(figsize=(15, 5))\n",
    "faked.plot.plot_pupil(show_events=False)\n",
    "plt.plot(tx/1000, real_baseline, label=\"baseline\")\n",
    "plt.vlines(event_onsets/1000, *plt.ylim(), color=\"grey\", alpha=0.5)\n",
    "plt.legend();"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "6336cbe9",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The orange line is the tonic, baseline component. At each event (grey lines), a scaled response kernel is added. The challenge is to extract both the size of the response and the baseline value at each event when only using the measured pupil data (the blue line).\n",
    "\n",
    "## Traditional approaches for disentangling tonic and phasic components\n",
    "\n",
    "One common way to analyse pupillometric data on the trial-by-trial level is to extract the average signal just before an event (as a measure of the baseline) and some time after the event (as a measure of the pupil's response). In `pypillometry`, this is implemented by `stat_per_event()`, which summarizes the signal in a time window around each event.\n",
    "\n",
    "For example, the following code extracts\n",
    "\n",
    "- the average signal from 200 ms before each event until the event (`0`) as baseline\n",
    "- the average signal from 800 ms until 1200 ms after each event as a measure of the response\n",
    "\n",
    "The baseline is then subtracted from the response:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "id": "763d7a07",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {

    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {

       "        1064.03141911, 1056.86661384, 1091.24004593, 1054.12046947,\n",
       "        1070.96222088, 1139.40891598, 1113.25888123, 1195.99348093,\n",

       "        1219.56578743, 1148.34374671, 1237.91395018, 1177.00180163,\n",
       "        1044.6882333 ,  956.96898122,  935.12733253,  969.56222201,\n",
       "        1020.253291  , 1013.06523706, 1091.89257587, 1113.22617499,\n",
       "        1156.46164584, 1189.72445557, 1153.85375071, 1144.32535071,\n",
       "        1078.47147651, 1110.182412  , 1058.94757395, 1006.90644063,\n",
       "        1025.38538538, 1005.60095871,  992.93209897,  991.09570187,\n",
       "         951.00503493, 1040.14332618,  977.77872015, 1004.7527711 ,\n",

     "execution_count": 4,

   ],
   "source": [
    "baseline = faked.stat_per_event(event_select=\"event\", window=(-200, 0) * u.ms)\n",
    "response = faked.stat_per_event(event_select=\"event\", window=(800, 1200) * u.ms)\n",
    "baseline"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "5c3c6727",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The result contains one array per eye and variable, with one value per event. We subtract the baseline from the response:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "67d6e76d",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-10T13:34:36.405450Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-10T13:34:36.405124Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-10T13:34:36.408061Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-10T13:34:36.407362Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "baseline = baseline[\"left_pupil\"]\n",
    "response = response[\"left_pupil\"] - baseline"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "2e27a6af",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "`stat_per_event()` supports selecting specific events (`event_select=`) and any summary function (`statfct=`, default is `numpy.mean`). Masked data (e.g., blinks) is ignored when computing the statistic, so the function has to handle masked arrays (e.g., `np.ma.median` instead of `np.median`):"
   ]
  },
  {

    "faked.stat_per_event(event_select=\"event\", window=(-200, 0) * u.ms, statfct=np.ma.median)"

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e201b621",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Advanced methods for tonic/phasic component estimation\n",
    "\n",
    "The simple method above is appealing for its simplicity but has severe limitations. Most importantly, multiple overlapping pupillary responses can \"look like\" baseline fluctuations when added together, thereby artificially inflating baseline estimates, particularly when events are spaced closely in time (\"fast paradigms\"). For that reason, we developed specialized algorithms to disentangle tonic and phasic components of the pupillometric signal.\n",
    "\n",
    "The algorithm uses an iterative procedure to remove an initial estimate of the responses from the signal to continue to estimate the underlying baseline. Details about how this algorithm works and which parameters it supports are available in [Mittner & Groot (2025)](https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-025-02755-7).\n",
    "\n",
    "The functionality is implemented in `pupil.estimate_baseline()` and `pupil.estimate_response()`. The response estimation depends on the estimated baseline, hence `pupil.estimate_baseline()` should be called first. Both functions are slow for high sampling rates, so it is a good idea to low-pass filter and downsample the data first (here, the simulated data already has a sampling rate of 50 Hz):"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 7,
   "id": "cd2dbfdc",
   "metadata": {

   "source": [
    "d = faked | pp.pupil.estimate_baseline() | pp.pupil.estimate_response()"

  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "88153fc8",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Here, we allowed the two shape parameters of the response kernel, `npar` and `tmax`, to vary freely together with the amplitudes of the responses. This allows an individualized shape of the pupillary response for each subject (which appears reasonable given the results in Hoeks & Levelt, 1993) but may take a long time to optimize and can result in pathological solutions. In that case, one or both of the parameters can be fixed, for example to reasonable group-level values (e.g., `pupil.estimate_response(npar=10.1, tmax=930)`).\n",
    "\n",
    "After running these methods, the baseline is stored as a new variable `baseline` and the predicted response as variable `response`:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 8,
   "id": "bccf6ce9",
   "metadata": {

    }

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "63e24e54",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "We can plot the estimated baseline and the full model (baseline+response) together with the data and the real baseline:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 10,
   "id": "11cded50",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-10T13:34:41.967069Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-10T13:34:41.966661Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-10T13:34:42.361633Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-10T13:34:42.360433Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 1500x500 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "plt.figure(figsize=(15, 5))\n",
    "plt.plot(d.tx/1000, d[\"left\", \"pupil\"], label=\"data\")\n",
    "plt.plot(d.tx/1000, real_baseline, label=\"real baseline\")\n",
    "plt.plot(d.tx/1000, d[\"left\", \"baseline\"], label=\"estimated baseline\")\n",
    "plt.plot(d.tx/1000, d[\"left\", \"baseline\"] + d[\"left\", \"response\"], label=\"model (baseline+response)\")\n",
    "plt.xlabel(\"seconds\")\n",
    "plt.legend();"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "77f771d0",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The estimated baseline is more wiggly than the real one but gives a considerably better estimate than the traditional method. The overall fit of the model is excellent (which is to be expected for simulated data).\n",
    "\n",
    "We can quantify how well the baseline estimation works relative to the traditional method by comparing both to the \"ground truth\" which is available for simulated data. We get the real and estimated baseline at each event onset with `stat_per_event()`:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 11,
   "id": "5157662c",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-10T13:34:42.365341Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-10T13:34:42.365064Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-10T13:34:42.429914Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-10T13:34:42.428803Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# store the real baseline as a variable so that we can use stat_per_event()\n",
    "d.data[\"left_realbaseline\"] = real_baseline\n",
    "\n",
    "at_onset = (0, 1000/fs) * u.ms   # one sample at the event onset\n",
    "real_baseline_ev = d.stat_per_event(event_select=\"event\", window=at_onset)[\"left_realbaseline\"]\n",
    "novel_baseline = d.stat_per_event(event_select=\"event\", window=at_onset)[\"left_baseline\"]\n",
    "novel_response = d.params[\"response\"][\"left_pupil\"][\"coef\"]\n",
    "\n",
    "traditional_baseline = baseline\n",
    "traditional_response = response"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "fbd326c4",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "and compare them by means of the correlation between the estimated and the real values:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 12,
   "id": "f0c02083",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-10T13:34:42.433859Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-10T13:34:42.433580Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-10T13:34:42.451268Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-10T13:34:42.450328Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Traditional method:\n",
      "Baseline: Corr(trad, real) = 0.9552897127692387\n",
      "Response: Corr(trad, real) = 0.4355020295417933\n",
      "\n",
      "Novel method:\n",
      "Baseline: Corr(nov, real) = 0.9695993602751325\n",
      "Response: Corr(nov, real) = 0.6044710168795537\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "print(\"Traditional method:\")\n",
    "print(\"Baseline: Corr(trad, real) =\", scipy.stats.pearsonr(traditional_baseline, real_baseline_ev)[0])\n",
    "print(\"Response: Corr(trad, real) =\", scipy.stats.pearsonr(traditional_response, real_response_coef)[0])\n",
    "print(\"\\nNovel method:\")\n",
    "print(\"Baseline: Corr(nov, real) =\", scipy.stats.pearsonr(novel_baseline, real_baseline_ev)[0])\n",
    "print(\"Response: Corr(nov, real) =\", scipy.stats.pearsonr(novel_response, real_response_coef)[0])"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "67db0c58",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The correlations are higher for the novel method than for the traditional method. More detailed simulation studies are reported in [Mittner & Groot (2025)](https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-025-02755-7).\n",
    "\n",
    "The parameters of the baseline estimation are described in the API documentation of `pp.signal.baseline_envelope_iter_bspline()` and, in more detail, in [Mittner & Groot (2025)](https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-025-02755-7).\n",
    "\n",
    "The parameters of the response estimation are described in the API documentation of `pp.signal.pupil_response()`."
   ]
  }
